details:
Avatar display limits can currently only be set against the overall Performance Rank (Excellent through Very Poor). That rank is determined by whichever single metric is worst.

The result is that an avatar that only exceeds the triangle budget, and an avatar that exceeds every budget, both land in the same bucket. Setting the threshold strictly hides the harmless one; setting it loosely shows the harmful one. In practice users end up choosing between hiding everything and showing everything, which is not what the rank system is meant to enable.

Request

Allow thresholds to be set per metric rather than against the aggregate:

Triangles

Material slots, skinned mesh count, mesh count

Texture memory (VRAM)

Bones, PhysBone components, affected transforms, colliders, contacts

Particle system totals and collision usage

Cloth vertices

Audio sources

Lights

Ideally each with three options: unlimited, a numeric threshold, or "disable this component only." The third option matters — it would allow showing an avatar while suppressing just its PhysBones or particles, rather than hiding the whole thing.

VRAM is the highest priority

Texture memory behaves differently from the other metrics: exceeding it causes crashes and out-of-memory terminations rather than degraded framerate. If only one metric gets per-metric control, this is the one. Right now there's no way to specifically exclude avatars that are heavy purely on textures.

Presets per situation

Having a single global configuration is itself a limitation. A crowded event instance and a small photo instance need different settings, and there's no way to switch between them short of reconfiguring by hand.

Multiple saved presets with manual switching would cover most of this. Automatic switching based on instance population would be better, but is not required for the feature to be useful.

Interaction with trust ranks

Safety settings already vary shader, particle, and animation permissions by trust rank, but performance thresholds do not. Being able to allow heavier avatars for friends while restricting others would follow the existing model.
title: Per-metric avatar performance gating instead of a single aggregate rank
